builders.angle: MEASURE EVERY OBJECT. Fix 1 is your round: the dimension table, and an audit of what is already built against it. The height field is in metres so this is checkable, not a matter of taste -- go and find every form whose measurements are wrong and correct it, starting with the Foyer's staircase (riser 0.17-0.19, going 0.25-0.30, so the rake is ~33 degrees and CONSTANT; handrail 0.90-1.00 above the pitch line; baluster gap under 0.10) and the Crypt's loculi (a 0.60 x 0.40 opening, not a 1.35 m recess). Then fix 2: straight lines where the thing is straight and regular spacing where it is regular -- the Graveyard's roof needs a ridge, straight eaves and a constant pitch instead of two smoothstep humps. Put the metre figure you used beside the table's figure for every object, in notes_for_merger. Do not touch a palette.

MAKE EVERY OBJECT NAMEABLE. Judges are being asked to point at each thing in the frame and say what it is, and the ones that fail today are named in the brief: the Greenhouse's planting reads as cauliflower, the Hedge Maze's hedges as mossy sarcophagi, the Study's shelving as scaffolding, the Graveyard's fence palings as traffic cones, the Foyer's chest and armchair and wardrobe as pale grey slabs. Take those in that order and make each one recognisably the thing it is supposed to be, built the way that thing is built -- a hedge is a 1.8 m mass with a scalloped top, planting has leaves and stems and a rim, shelves have board thickness and uprights and things standing on them at different heights. FOLIAGE is the weakest of the six wall modes and its three recorded failure modes are in fix 9; check anything you add to a foliage mass against masonry first. A green glasshouse is fine -- Josh has ruled -- so spend nothing on colour.

A LINE ROUND EVERY FORM, AND LIGHT ENOUGH TO SEE IT BY. Fix 4 first: we ink the HOLLOWS of relief steps and nothing else, so a form standing IN FRONT of another form has no line between them -- prop silhouettes, arch mouldings, the stair, railings, headstones, the wall/floor junction. Both judges raised it on every screen and one called it the single cheapest thing that would move these from render to painting. Mind the hierarchy: mmDrawn saturates at 0.26 of height per pixel, so repeating joints belong at 0.10-0.21 and big forms at 0.5-0.9. Then fix 8 as CRAFT and not as colour-matching: our rooms are two to three times darker in the median than the samples with half the lit area and light MORE concentrated, so a few small pools carry everything and the rest of the room is unlit rather than dim -- and a room nobody can see the objects in fails the round's first question. A floor is nearer the light and flatter than a wall, which is why his pictures are brightest at the bottom and ours across the middle. Also fix 7: on combat the balustrade's hairlines cross behind the enemy nameplates.
